items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone)] pub struct Module { pub core : emela_core :: Module , pub functions : Arena < Function > , pub stage : Stage , pub error_shows : Vec < (EnumId , FnId) > , }
items.docs:
A LIR module. It owns the Core module it was made from: variables' Core types are IDs of its
type table, and constructors, enums and effects are those of its definitions. The Core
functions are not used (the LIR functions replace them).

Owned rather than borrowed: a reference would put a lifetime parameter on every type and pass
of the crate.
Which passes have run, and so which constructs the functions may hold.

The generated show function of each error enum, made by `from_core` for every error enum
without type parameters that the functions construct, called or not: the error's display
(`emela_core::Module::error_display`) decides between the structural `show$E`, the function
of its Show impl, and `name$E` (the name only) for an error that does not satisfy Show.
Backends show a failure that reaches the entry with it (`error: NotFound(id: 1)`,
`error: Retry`, `[dyn.error]`); which enum arrives is only known at run time.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , Copy , PartialEq , Eq , PartialOrd , Ord , Hash)] pub enum Stage { Flow , ClosuresConverted , DefectsExplicit , StateMachines , RefCounted , }
attributes: # [derive (Debug , Clone , Copy , PartialEq , Eq , PartialOrd , Ord , Hash)]
items.docs:
The stage of a LIR module. The Flow IR and the Heap IR share the data types; each pass of the
Heap IR forbids some constructs and allows new ones, and the verifier checks the invariants of
the module's stage. Later stages include the earlier ones' invariants.

Made by `from_core`: closures nested in their functions, `defect` and `protect` with
implicit unwinding, no reference counting.

Closures lifted to functions taking their record as the environment
([`Value::MakeClosure`], [`Value::EnvGet`]); no [`Value::Closure`] or [`Value::FnRef`].

Defects and cleanups made explicit control: calls that may raise a defect have a landing
(`on_defect`), failure edges have landings ([`OnFail::Handle`]), [`Term::Unwind`] leaves a
function with the pending defect, and the cleanups of `protect` are copied onto every way
out of its body. No [`Stmt::Protect`], [`Term::Defect`], [`OnFail::Break`] or
[`OnFail::Propagate`].

Suspending functions made resumable state machines: every value of a suspending function
that may come back suspended has an `on_suspend` edge ([`Suspend`]) that saves the
variables still needed into a heap frame, and fairness yields ([`RuntimeOp::Yield`],
[`RuntimeOp::YieldPerform`]) come before suspending calls.

Reference counts explicit: [`Stmt::Dup`] and [`Stmt::Drop`] make every owned reference be
consumed exactly once on every path (see `heap::rc` for who owns what).

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone)] pub struct Function { pub name : String , pub exported : bool , pub params : Vec < VarId > , pub ret : TypeId , pub fails : bool , pub suspends : bool , pub constant : bool , pub external : Option < External > , pub env : Option < Vec < TypeId > > , pub defects : bool , pub body : Option < SeqId > , pub vars : Arena < VarData > , pub stmts : Arena < Stmt > , pub seqs : Arena < Seq > , pub labels : Arena < LabelData > , }
items.docs: A function, with its own arenas.
Unique in the module.

Only parameters with a representation: a parameter of type `()` or `Never` has no variable
and no argument. The evidence table, if taken, is an ordinary last parameter (`ref`, Core
type `Evidence`).

The Core type of the return value. The function returns nothing if its representation is
[`Repr::Void`].

Whether it may fail: `fail` and the `on_fail fail` edge are allowed only then, and direct
calls to it must have a failure edge.
Whether it may suspend (`emela_core::Function::suspends`).
A const's value (`emela_core::Function::constant`).
For an external function, the host function; `body` is then `None`.

For a function lifted from a closure (Heap IR), the Core types of the captured values, in
the order of [`Value::MakeClosure::captures`]. Its first parameter is then the environment:
the closure record itself (`ref`, with the closure's function type as its Core type),
borrowed for the call. [`Value::EnvGet`] reads the captures from it.

Heap IR, from [`Stage::DefectsExplicit`]: whether a call may come back with a pending
defect, so that calls to it need a defect landing. External functions may (a host
exception is a defect, spec 12.5).
The body. Every path ends in a terminator other than [`Term::Yield`].

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq , Eq)] pub struct VarData { pub hint : String , pub repr : Repr , pub ty : TypeId , }
items.docs:
A variable. Defined exactly once (as a parameter, a statement's destination, a loop variable or
a closure parameter) and never assigned again.
A naming hint for output; need not be unique.

How the value is held. Never [`Repr::Void`]: values without a representation get no
variable.
The Core type, an ID of the module's Core type table. `repr` is `repr_of` this type.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq , Eq)] pub struct LabelData { pub hint : String , }
items.docs: A label of a [`Stmt::Block`], the target of [`Term::Break`] and [`OnFail::Break`].

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq)] pub struct Seq { pub stmts : Vec < StmtId > , pub term : Term , }
items.docs: A sequence of statements run in order, then its terminator.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq)] pub enum Term { Yield (Option < Operand >) , Return (Option < Operand >) , Fail (Operand) , Break { label : LabelId , value : Option < Operand > , } , Recur (Vec < Operand >) , Defect (Operand , Option < String >) , Unwind , Unreachable , }
items.docs: How a sequence ends.

Leaves the sequence normally, giving the value of the enclosing compound statement: the
arm's value for `if` and `switch`, the block's value, the loop's value (leaving the loop),
the protected body's value. Without a value when the statement has no destination. Not
allowed at the end of a function or closure body, and a cleanup ends with it without value.
Returns from the enclosing function or closure. Without a value when it returns nothing.
Fails the enclosing function or closure with the error value (`ref`).

items.declaration: Break { label : LabelId , value : Option < Operand > , }
items.docs: Leaves the enclosing block with the label, giving its value.

Starts the next iteration of the innermost enclosing loop with new values for its
variables. It cannot cross a `protect` or a closure: in Core the body of `with` is not in
tail position either, and a closure is another body.

Raises a defect with the message (a string operand, since some messages, such as those of
`assert`, are built at run time), unwinding through the cleanups to the caller. The
second field is the location of a failed assert (`<path>:<line>:<column>`,
`[test.assert]`), kept outside the message. Flow IR only: the Heap IR makes the unwinding
explicit with [`RuntimeOp::Defect`] (or [`RuntimeOp::DefectAt`]) and [`Term::Unwind`].

Heap IR: returns from the function with the pending defect (the caller's defect landing
runs). The function's result is not given (backends return any value).
Control never gets here (after a call that does not return, such as `panic`).

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq)] pub enum Stmt { Let { dst : Option < VarId > , value : Value , on_defect : Option < SeqId > , on_suspend : Option < Suspend > , } , If { dst : Option < VarId > , cond : Operand , then : SeqId , else_ : SeqId , } , Switch { dst : Option < VarId > , on : SwitchOn , cases : Vec < Case > , default : Option < SeqId > , } , Loop { dst : Option < VarId > , vars : Vec < VarId > , inits : Vec < Operand > , body : SeqId , } , Block { dst : Option < VarId > , label : LabelId , body : SeqId , } , Protect { dst : Option < VarId > , body : SeqId , cleanup : SeqId , } , Dup (VarId) , Drop (VarId) , }
items.docs:
A statement. Each optional `dst` is the variable defined by the statement, visible to the
statements after it in the same sequence (and the sequences nested in those). `None` when the
value has no representation or is unused.

A compound statement that gives a value (`if`, `switch`, `block`, `loop`, `protect`) has its
result variable as `dst`, and its arms end with `yield v`, rather than declaring the variable
first and assigning it in each arm. So every variable is defined exactly once: the verifier
checks definition before use by scope alone, and liveness and reference counting stay simple.
WASM maps it to the result of `block` and `if`, C to an assignment of a declared variable.

items.declaration: Let { dst : Option < VarId > , value : Value , on_defect : Option < SeqId > , on_suspend : Option < Suspend > , }
items.docs:
`dst = value`．`on_defect` (Heap IR) is the landing run instead of the rest of the sequence
when the value (a call, builtin or concurrency operation that may raise a defect) comes
back with a pending defect. It does not see `dst` and cannot yield. `on_suspend` (Heap IR,
from [`Stage::StateMachines`], in suspending functions) is what happens when the value
comes back suspended.

items.declaration: If { dst : Option < VarId > , cond : Operand , then : SeqId , else_ : SeqId , }
items.docs: Runs `then` if `cond` (an `i32`) is not zero, else `else_`.

items.declaration: Switch { dst : Option < VarId > , on : SwitchOn , cases : Vec < Case > , default : Option < SeqId > , }
items.docs:
Runs the case matching the scrutinee, or `default`. Without a default, a tag switch must
cover every constructor; a literal switch always has a default.

items.declaration: Loop { dst : Option < VarId > , vars : Vec < VarId > , inits : Vec < Operand > , body : SeqId , }
items.docs:
Binds `vars` to `inits` and runs `body`; [`Term::Recur`] rebinds them and runs it again, and
[`Term::Yield`] leaves the loop with its value. Made from `emela_core::Expr::Loop`.

items.declaration: Block { dst : Option < VarId > , label : LabelId , body : SeqId , }
items.docs:
Runs `body`; [`Term::Break`] with `label` from inside leaves it early. The receiver of
`escape` and the target of failure edges.

items.declaration: Protect { dst : Option < VarId > , body : SeqId , cleanup : SeqId , }
items.docs:
Runs `body`, then `cleanup` however `body` is left (value, break, return, failure, defect,
unwinding while suspended). `cleanup` cannot leave by any other way than its end. Made from
the releases of `with` (spec 14.2).

Heap IR: adds a reference to the `ref` variable's value. Backends expand it to a call of
the runtime (or an inline increment); static data is marked so that it is never counted.

Heap IR: gives up a reference to the `ref` variable's value, freeing it (and dropping what
it holds) when it was the last one.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq , Eq)] pub struct Suspend { pub state : u32 , pub saved : Vec < VarId > , }
items.docs:
The suspension edge of a value in a suspending function (Heap IR, from
[`Stage::StateMachines`]): a resume point of the function's state machine.

The value (a suspending call, a waiting concurrency operation or a fairness yield) either comes
back as usual (fast path: nothing is allocated, the variables stay in locals), or comes back
suspended. Then a frame of the function is allocated with `state` and the `saved` variables
(moved into it), pushed onto the continuation being captured, and the function returns
(suspended) to its caller, which does the same up to the runtime's driver loop. When the
runtime resumes the frame, the function is entered again with the frame: the saved variables
are restored and control continues right after the value as if it had come back with the
resumed input (its value in `dst`, or a pending failure or defect for the landings).
The resume point, unique in the function (numbered from 0).

The variables saved in the frame, in slot order: every variable live after the value (on
any way on, the landings included) and the references the value borrows, so that the
resumed function owns exactly what the uninterrupted one owns after the value.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , Copy , PartialEq , Eq)] pub enum SwitchOn { Tag (VarId) , Lit (VarId) , }
items.docs: What a switch looks at.
The constructor of an enum value; cases are [`CaseKey::Variant`].
An `i32` or `i64` value; cases are [`CaseKey::Lit`] of the same representation.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq)] pub struct Case { pub key : CaseKey , pub body : SeqId , }
# [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq)] pub enum CaseKey { Variant (usize) , Lit (Const) , }

items.docs: An index into the enum's `variants`.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq)] pub enum Operand { Var (VarId) , Const (Const) , }
items.docs: An argument: a variable or a constant (ANF).

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq)] pub enum Const { Int (i32) , Int64 (i64) , Float (f64) , Bool (bool) , String (String) , Unit , }
items.docs: A constant.

The placeholder for `()` in a slot of a container: a constructor field, a tuple element, a
list element, a cell's contents or a concurrency operation's argument whose type has no
representation. It keeps the slot (so `List[()]` keeps its length and field indices stay
Core's); backends store any word there. Its representation is [`Repr::Void`], so it is
accepted only in such slots.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq)] pub enum Value { Const (Const) , Prim { op : PrimOp , ty : PrimTy , args : Vec < Operand > , } , Call { callee : Callee , args : Vec < Operand > , suspends : bool , on_fail : Option < OnFail > , } , Builtin { op : Builtin , args : Vec < Operand > , } , Make { ctor : CtorRef , args : Vec < Operand > , } , Field { base : VarId , ctor : CtorRef , index : usize , } , Tag (VarId) , Tuple (Vec < Operand >) , TupleGet { base : VarId , index : usize , } , List { elems : Vec < Operand > , tail : Option < Operand > , } , ListIsEmpty (VarId) , ListHead (VarId) , ListTail (VarId) , FnRef (FnId) , Closure (Box < Closure >) , MakeClosure { function : FnId , captures : Vec < VarId > , } , EnvGet { env : VarId , index : usize , } , EvLookup { ev : VarId , effect : EffectId , } , EvExtend { base : Option < VarId > , bindings : Vec < (EffectId , VarId) > , } , Handler { name : String , effect : EffectId , ops : Vec < VarId > , } , Fiber { op : FiberOp , args : Vec < Operand > , on_fail : Option < OnFail > , } , IsError { error : VarId , enum_id : EnumId , } , AsError { error : VarId , enum_id : EnumId , } , Runtime { op : RuntimeOp , args : Vec < Operand > , } , Coerce (VarId) , }
items.docs:
The right-hand side of [`Stmt::Let`]. Arguments are operands, and values that must be
variables (bases, callees, closures' captures) are [`VarId`]s.

items.declaration: Prim { op : PrimOp , ty : PrimTy , args : Vec < Operand > , }
items.docs: A numeric operation or comparison.

items.declaration: Call { callee : Callee , args : Vec < Operand > , suspends : bool , on_fail : Option < OnFail > , }
items.docs:
A call. Arguments are the callee's parameters that have a representation, with the
evidence table last if it takes one. `on_fail` is the failure edge, present exactly when
the callee may fail. `suspends` means the same as `emela_core::Expr::Call::suspends`.

items.declaration: Builtin { op : Builtin , args : Vec < Operand > , }
items.docs: A builtin. After monomorphisation, so without type arguments. Builtins do not fail.

items.declaration: Make { ctor : CtorRef , args : Vec < Operand > , }
items.docs:
An enum value. Arguments are the constructor's fields in field order; a field without
representation gets [`Const::Unit`].

items.declaration: Field { base : VarId , ctor : CtorRef , index : usize , }
items.docs:
Field `index` (in field definition order) of `base`, which must be a value of `ctor`. A
field without representation has nothing to read (no destination).
The constructor index of an enum value (`i32`).
A tuple. An element without representation gets [`Const::Unit`].
Element `index` of a tuple.

items.declaration: List { elems : Vec < Operand > , tail : Option < Operand > , }
items.docs: `[a, b]` or `[a, b, ..tail]`. Elements without representation are [`Const::Unit`].
Whether the list is empty (`i32`).

The first element of a non-empty list (nothing to read, so no destination, for elements
without representation).
The rest of a non-empty list.

A top-level function used as a value. Flow IR only (closure conversion makes it a
[`Value::MakeClosure`] of a wrapper).
A closure. Its body is nested here. Flow IR only (closure conversion lifts it).

items.declaration: MakeClosure { function : FnId , captures : Vec < VarId > , }
items.docs:
Heap IR: a closure record `{function, captures…}`. `function` is a lifted function (its
`env` lists the captures' Core types); calling the record (`call_indirect`, or `call_op`
through a handler) calls `function` with the record itself as the first argument (the
environment), then the call's arguments. The record is the environment: captures live in
it directly, so making a closure is one allocation.

Heap IR: capture `index` of the environment `env`, the first parameter of a lifted
function.
The current handler of the effect in the evidence table (`emela_core::Expr::Use`).

items.declaration: EvExtend { base : Option < VarId > , bindings : Vec < (EffectId , VarId) > , }
items.docs:
A new evidence table: `base` (or an empty table) plus `bindings`, later bindings winning
(`emela_core::Expr::Provide`).

items.declaration: Handler { name : String , effect : EffectId , ops : Vec < VarId > , }
items.docs:
A handler value (`emela_core::Expr::Handler`): one closure per operation of the effect, in
declaration order.

items.declaration: Fiber { op : FiberOp , args : Vec < Operand > , on_fail : Option < OnFail > , }
items.docs:
A concurrency operation (spec chapter 11), done by the runtime. Arguments are as for
`emela_core::Expr::Fiber`, with [`Const::Unit`] for one without representation. `on_fail`
is present exactly when the operation may fail (`FiberOp::fails`).

Whether the caught failure `error` (`ref`) is a value of the error enum (`i32`). Used by the
arms of `escape`, where failures of different error enums arrive at the same block.

The caught failure `error` seen as a value of the error enum, after [`Value::IsError`] said
it is one. Defines a variable of that enum type.

items.declaration: Runtime { op : RuntimeOp , args : Vec < Operand > , }
items.docs: An operation of the runtime that the language has no builtin for.

The variable's value at the destination's Core type, which differs from the variable's:
a function value used at a function type with other `fails` / `suspends` flags (a smaller
E or R used where a larger one is expected, spec 9.2), or a value entering or leaving
`Any`. The representations must agree unless one side is `Any` (then the value is boxed or
unboxed). Made where a `let` binds a value to a local of another type: the failure edge
and `suspends` of a call through a function value follow the called variable's type, so
the local must have its own type or the verifier disagrees. Backends whose calling
conventions depend on those flags adapt the value here.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , Copy , PartialEq , Eq)] pub enum RuntimeOp { ShowString , DebugPrint , Retire , Defect , DefectAt , DefectTake , DefectResume , Hold , Unhold , Yield , YieldPerform , }
items.docs:
Runtime operations that Core has no builtin for, made by the conversion from Core.

They live here rather than as Core builtins because a Core builtin also needs an `@intrinsic`
declaration in the bundled sources and an implementation in the JS backend.

`(String) -> String`: a string shown inside a value or by `dbg` (spec 10.6), in `"` with
the escapes of `$showString` in the JS runtime.
`(String) -> ()`: writes the line to stderr (`dbg`).

`(handler, String) -> ()`: marks the handler value released, so that each of its operations
is the defect `handler <name> was used after release` from then on (spec 8.6). The string
is the handler's name.

`(String) -> ()`: makes the message the pending defect. If a defect is already pending (a
release failing while unwinding, spec 14.4), the message becomes a note of it instead.
Heap IR; a [`Term::Unwind`] (through the cleanups) follows.

`(String, String) -> ()`: [`RuntimeOp::Defect`] for a failed assert, whose defect carries
the location (the second string, a constant) outside its message (`[test.assert]`). The
location stays with the defect when a note is added to its message. Heap IR.

`() -> ref`: takes the pending defect out, so that a cleanup runs with no defect pending.
Heap IR.

`(ref) -> ()`: puts back a defect taken by [`RuntimeOp::DefectTake`] as the pending one.
A defect raised meanwhile (by the cleanup) becomes a note of it (spec 14.4: the first
defect is the result). Consumes the argument. Heap IR.

`() -> ()`: marks the start of a release that may suspend: the current fiber is not
interrupted until [`RuntimeOp::Unhold`] (spec 11.4).
`() -> ()`: the end of a release started with [`RuntimeOp::Hold`].

`() -> ()`: a fairness yield before a suspending call (spec 11.1). Spends one unit of the
running fiber's budget; when it runs out, the fiber suspends and goes to the end of the
queue (and a pending interruption is delivered instead, as a defect). Heap IR, in
suspending functions only.

`() -> ()`: [`RuntimeOp::Yield`] before a call of a `suspend fn` operation, which also
delivers a pending interruption (spec 11.4: the call is a suspension point). Heap IR.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq)] pub struct Closure { pub params : Vec < VarId > , pub captures : Vec < VarId > , pub body : SeqId , pub suspends : bool , }
items.docs:
A closure value. It shares the function's arenas. Its body may use the variables of the
enclosing bodies only if they are listed in `captures`. Its Core type is that of the
statement's destination, which gives its parameters, `suspends` and `fails`.
With the evidence table last if it takes one (the closure's Core type says).
The variables of the enclosing bodies the body uses, each once, in first-use order.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq)] pub enum Callee { Direct (FnId) , Indirect (VarId) , Op { handler : VarId , effect : EffectId , op : usize , } , }

items.docs: A top-level function.
A function value (`ref`).

items.declaration: Op { handler : VarId , effect : EffectId , op : usize , }
items.docs: Operation `op` (an index into `EffectDef::ops`) of the handler value `handler`.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , Copy , PartialEq , Eq)] pub enum OnFail { Break (LabelId) , Propagate , Handle { error : VarId , body : SeqId } , }
items.docs: Where a failing call goes. The error value (`ref`) goes with it.
Leaves the enclosing block with the label, giving the error as its value. Flow IR only.
Fails the enclosing function or closure (as [`Term::Fail`]). Flow IR only.

Heap IR: binds the error to `error` and runs the landing `body`, which cannot yield (it
breaks, fails, returns or unwinds). Each failing call has its own landing, so the
reference counting pass can release what differs between them.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , Copy , PartialEq , Eq)] pub enum PrimOp { Add , Sub , Mul , Div , Rem , Neg , Not , Eq , Ne , Lt , Le , Gt , Ge , }
items.docs:
Numeric operations and comparisons. Comparisons give an `i32` (0 or 1); the others give the
operand type.
For `i32` and `i64`, Int's division (spec 16.1): a defect when dividing by zero.
Unary.
Unary; the logical not of an `i32` truth value (Bool).

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , Copy , PartialEq , Eq)] pub enum PrimTy { I32 , I64 , F64 , String , }
items.docs:
The operand type of a [`PrimOp`]: a representation, plus strings, which are compared by
contents (only comparisons).

Structural equality is not a primitive: like showing, it becomes calls of functions generated
per type (`eq$Point`).

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , Copy , PartialEq , Eq , Hash)] pub enum Repr { I32 , I64 , F64 , Ref , Void , }
items.docs:
How a value is held. Memory layout (field offsets, pointer width) is not decided here; that is
the backend's.
A 32-bit integer: Int, Bool, and the tag of an enum whose constructors take no arguments.
A reference to a heap value or a host value.
No value: `()` and `Never`. No variable has it; a function returning it returns nothing.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , Copy , PartialEq , Eq , Hash)] pub enum Builtin { StringLength , StringByteSize , StringAppend , StringContains , StringStartsWith , StringEndsWith , StringSplit , StringChars , StringJoin , StringTrim , StringCodePoints , StringFromCodePoint , ShowNested , IntToString , IntParse , IntCheckedAdd , IntBitAnd , IntBitOr , IntBitXor , IntBitNot , IntShiftLeft , IntShiftRight , IntShiftRightUnsigned , Int64FromInt , Int64ToString , Int64ToInt , Int64BitAnd , Int64BitOr , Int64BitXor , Int64BitNot , Int64ShiftLeft , Int64ShiftRight , Int64ShiftRightUnsigned , FloatToString , FloatFromInt , FloatParse , FloatFloor , FloatCeil , FloatRound , FloatTruncate , BytesFromList , BytesToList , BytesSize , BytesGet , BytesSlice , BytesConcat , BytesEncodeUtf8 , BytesDecodeValidUtf8 , Panic , Todo , Dbg , Inspect , CellNew , CellGet , CellSet , ShowString , DebugPrint , AssertFail , }

items.docs: `String.length`: the number of grapheme clusters.
`String.byte_size`: the number of bytes in UTF-8.
`String.append(a, b)`．
`String.split(s, sep)`. An empty separator splits into graphemes.
`String.chars`: one string per grapheme cluster.
`List.join(parts, sep)`, formerly `String.join`. It makes a String.
`String.trim`: removes leading and trailing Unicode White_Space.
`String.code_points`.
`String.from_code_point`. `None` if not a Unicode scalar value.

`String.show_nested` (`@internal`): the Show of a value inside another value (spec 10.6),
for the Show impls in core. Monomorphization replaces it with [`Builtin::ShowString`] for a
String and with a call of `Show.show` for any other type, so backends never see it.

The body of `Int.parse`. Reads only decimal digits with an optional leading sign; anything
else, or out of range, is `None`.
`Int.checked_add`. `None` on overflow.
`Int.shift_left(n, by)`. Shift amounts as in `[api.int]`.
`Int.shift_right(n, by)`. Keeps the sign (arithmetic shift).
`Int.shift_right_unsigned(n, by)`. Fills the high bits with 0 (logical shift).
`Int64.to_int`. Keeps the low 32 bits.
`Float.from_int`. Every Int is exactly representable as a Float.

The body of `Float.parse`. Reads only the forms `to_string` writes; anything else is
`None`.
Ties round away from zero.
`Bytes.from_list`. `None` if an element is outside 0 to 255.
`Bytes.get(b, index)`. `None` if out of range or negative.

`Bytes.slice(b, from, to)`. Both ends are clamped to 0 to the size; empty if `from` is not
less than `to`.
`Bytes.encode_utf8`: the UTF-8 bytes of the string.

The private `decode_valid_utf8`: the string of bytes that `decode_utf8` has already
checked to be valid UTF-8. Backends need not check again.
`panic(message)`.
`todo()`. Raises a `not yet implemented` defect.

`dbg(value)`. Prints the debug display of the value to stderr on one line and returns the
value (spec 10.6). Takes no trait; what reaches a backend is shown by its structure
([`crate::mono`] rewrites the rest).

`inspect(value)`: the debug display of a value with Show (spec 10.6), a String quoted.
What reaches a backend is shown by its structure, which is its Show.
Makes a cell holding one value (the state of `State.run`, spec 8.8).
Replaces the cell's contents. The value is `()`.

A String shown inside another value: quoted and escaped (spec 10.6). What
[`Builtin::ShowNested`] becomes for a String, and what derived Show uses for a String field.

Prints the String as it is on one line to stderr. What `dbg` becomes for a value shown
through its Show impl (spec 10.6). The value is `()`.

`(message, location)`: the defect of a failed assert, with the location of the assert
expression outside the message (`[test.assert]`). What monomorphization makes of an assert
whose sides are shown through a written Show impl. The location is a string literal.

The per-target `@external` arguments, in written order.

What an `@external` points to in the host (spec 12.1). What a name means is up to the target's
backend.

One argument, `@external(js, "console.log")`: a name the host resolves on its own (a global
reference in JS).

A module the host finds by name (`node:fs`, `env`, `wasi:http/client`).

A file next to a project source (written starting with `./` or `../`), as an absolute path
resolved from the declaring source's directory.

A file bundled with the compiler (written in a bundled source starting with `./` or `../`),

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq , Eq)] pub struct EffectDef { pub name : String , pub decl : String , pub args : Vec < TypeId > , pub ops : Vec < OpDef > , pub label_of : Option < EffectId > , }
items.docs:
An effect (spec 8.1). An effect with type arguments is one `EffectDef` per instantiation
(`State[Int]` and `State[String]` are different effects), and the types of its operations are
the instantiated ones.
Unique in the module; used as the evidence table key.

The IR name of the effect declaration this instantiates (`State.State` for
`State.State[Int]`); the same as `name` for an effect without type parameters.

The type arguments of the instantiation, in the declaration's parameter order. Set type
arguments (`Scope[E, R]`, spec 11.2) have no IR type and are the placeholder `()`. A
`Type::Param(i)` is a type parameter of the function whose body uses the effect (the key
`State[$modify.0]` is used only in the body of `modify`), as in that function's local types.
In declaration order; indexed by `Callee::Op::op` and `Expr::Handler::ops`.

For a label (`effect AuditLog of Console`, issue #255), the effect it stands for. The label
is its own key in evidence tables, but its handler values are the base's: `Use` of a label
has type `Type::Handler(base)`, and a table binding of the label holds a handler of the
base. `ops` are the base's.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq , Eq)] pub struct OpDef { pub name : String , pub suspend : bool , pub type_params : usize , pub params : Vec < TypeId > , pub ret : TypeId , pub fails : bool , }
items.docs:
An effect operation (spec 8.1), with its types for the instantiation of its effect.

An operation may have type parameters of its own only in built-in effects (`fork[A]` and
`deferred[A]` of Scope, spec 8.1, 11.2). They are `Type::Param(0..type_params)` in `params` and
`ret`, instantiated per call by `Callee::Op::ty_args`. The type arguments of built-in effects
are sets (`Scope[E, R]`), so such an operation's types contain no other `Type::Param`. A
handler implements a generic operation for every instantiation at once, so its implementation
sees the operation's own type parameters as `Type::Any`.

Why type parameters rather than `Any` in the `OpDef` itself: so that the value of a call
(`Fiber[Int]` from `s.fork[Int](..)`) has a type the IR alone determines. The type checker
records the instantiation at the operation reference, so filling `Callee::Op::ty_args` costs
no more than for a direct call.

Whether it is a `suspend fn`. If true, the handler's implementation (a lambda in
`Expr::Handler::ops`) takes resume (`fn(ret) -> ()`) as its last argument and returns `()`,
and operation calls (`Callee::Op`) are suspending calls (spec 8.4, 14.5).
The number of the operation's own type parameters (see above); 0 outside built-in effects.

The declared parameters' types. For Scope's fork, the IR passes the child function wrapped
to take the evidence table as an ordinary parameter (`fn(evidence) -> A`, see
`lower/fiber.rs`), and the type says so.
Whether a call may fail: the operation's E is not empty (spec 7.2).

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone)] pub struct EnumDef { pub name : String , pub params : usize , pub variants : Vec < VariantDef > , pub error : bool , pub external : bool , }
items.docs: An enum definition. A `type` is an enum with one constructor.
The number of type parameters. `Type::Param(i)` in field types refers to the `i`th.

Whether it is an error declaration (spec 7.1): one constructor, no type parameters. It can
be passed to `Expr::Fail` and written in `Expr::Escape` arm patterns. Backends must
represent it so the error can be identified at run time.

Whether it is an `@external type` (spec 12.3): an opaque host value with no constructors,
which Emela only passes around (`Std.Fiber.Fiber` is one too, made by the runtime). Backends
represent its values as host handles. An enum without constructors that is not external
has no values.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone)] pub struct VariantDef { pub name : String , pub fields : VariantFields , pub tys : Vec < TypeId > , }

items.docs:
Field types, in `fields` order. Used to build show functions (the stand-in for Show) from
types.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq , Eq , Hash)] pub enum Type { Int , Int64 , Float , Bool , String , Bytes , Unit , Never , Tuple (Vec < TypeId >) , List (TypeId) , Enum (EnumId , Vec < TypeId >) , Param (usize) , Fn (FnType) , Handler (EffectId) , Evidence , Cell (TypeId) , FiberScope , Any , Set (SetSummary) , }
items.docs:
The structure of an IR type, with components as [`TypeId`]s. Used for showing (the stand-in
for Show), for builtins whose behavior depends on the type, and by backends that need value
representations.

The type checker's `emela_types::Ty` rewritten with IR names (`EnumId`, `EffectId`). No type
variables: a type variable left undetermined (an unused `None`'s `Option[?]`) becomes `Unit`,
as any representation behaves the same.

`Std.Bytes.Bytes` (`[api.std.bytes]`), the built-in type of an `@intrinsic` type
declaration. Immutable; the `Builtin::Bytes*` functions make and read it.
Two or more elements.
An enum / type application. The argument count is `EnumDef::params`.

The `i`th type parameter of the enclosing definition: the `EnumDef` in field types, the
function otherwise.
A function value (spec 10.6: cannot be shown).

A capability value (spec 8.2): the handler value of the effect, returned by `use X`
(`Expr::Use`). Cannot be shown or compared.

The capability value is the handler value itself, not a reference into a table. A
capability taken out earlier sits in a variable, so it keeps pointing at that handler even
when an inner `with` provides the effect again (`[effect.with]`), and a closure that
captures it (`[effect.use]`) only captures the variable.
An evidence table (`Expr::Provide`, spec 16.5).
A mutable cell holding a value of the type (the state of `State.run`, `Builtin::CellNew`).

The run-time scope that `FiberOp::Scope` passes to its body and `FiberOp::Fork` and
`FiberOp::Deferred` take (spec 11.2). Not Scope's capability value, which is a `Handler`.

A value whose type differs per use and is not tracked: inside Scope's handler, the child
function that fork receives (the `A` of `fork[A]`, spec 11.2) and the handles that
`FiberOp::Fork` and `FiberOp::Deferred` return. Only built-in effects have generic
operations (spec 8.1), and lowering builds their handlers. Backends give it a uniform
representation. A handler's implementation of a generic operation sees the operation's own
type parameters as `Any` too (`OpDef`).

[`crate::verify`] accepts `Any` where any type is expected and the other way round.

What decides calling conventions about an error or effect set: the argument of a set type
parameter (`R(f)` of `List.map`) in `ty_args` and in enum type arguments, and the E and R
of a function type with set type parameters ([`FnSets`]). Not the type of a value.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq , Eq , Hash , Default)] pub struct SetSummary { pub fails : bool , pub suspends : bool , pub ev : bool , pub params : Vec < TypeId > , }
items.docs:
An error or effect set reduced to what decides how a function with it is called
([`Type::Set`]). The flags are those of the set's elements other than set type parameters,
which are listed in `params` (as `Type::Param`, sorted, each once). With `params` empty, the
set is fully known.

The flags are worked out without knowing whether the set is an E or an R, so only the ones that
matter for its position are read: `fails` for an E, `suspends` and `ev` for an R.
The set is not empty (as an E: a call may fail).
As an R: a call may suspend (not Immediate, spec 9.5).
As an R: it has an element other than Async, so the function takes the evidence table.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , Copy , PartialEq , Eq , Hash)] pub struct FnSets { pub errors : TypeId , pub effects : TypeId , }
items.docs:
The E and R of a function type that contain set type parameters, as [`Type::Set`]s
([`FnType::sets`]).

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq , Eq , Hash)] pub struct FnType { pub params : Vec < TypeId > , pub ret : TypeId , pub fails : bool , pub suspends : bool , pub ev : bool , pub sets : Option < FnSets > , }
items.docs: A function type, with what decides how a value of it is called.
The declared parameters, without the evidence table.
Whether a call may fail (the E is not empty, spec 7.2); the same as `Expr::Call::fails`.

Whether a call may suspend (the R is not Immediate, spec 9.5); the same as
`Expr::Call::suspends` for `Callee::Indirect`.

Whether the function takes the evidence table as its last argument (the R has effects
other than Async, spec 16.5).

The E and R when they contain set type parameters of the enclosing definition (`R(f)`),
`None` otherwise. Then the flags above over-approximate every instantiation (a set type
parameter counts as failing and needing the evidence table; whether it may suspend follows
the suspending copy being lowered), and substituting known sets for the parameters
([`subst_type`]) makes them exact.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , PartialEq , Eq)] pub enum VariantFields { Unit , Positional (usize) , Named (Vec < String >) , }
items.docs: The three forms of variants.
`Red`
`Some(T)`. The value is the field count.
`Point { x: Int, y: Int }`. In definition order.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , Copy , PartialEq , Eq , Hash)] pub struct CtorRef { pub enum_id : EnumId , pub variant : usize , }

items.docs: An index into `EnumDef::variants`.

items.declaration: # [derive (Debug , Clone , Copy , PartialEq , Eq)] pub enum FiberOp { Scope { fails : bool } , Fork , Deferred , Join , Await { exit : EnumId } , Interrupt , Attempt { exit : EnumId , suspends : bool } , Complete , DeferredAwait , Poll , CauseKind { kind : EnumId } , CauseToString , CauseRaise { fails : bool } , }
items.docs:
Concurrency operations (spec chapter 11). The `args` of `Expr::Fiber` are in the order given
for each variant.

`Expr::Fiber` carries no `fails` / `suspends` marks of its own, unlike `Expr::Call`: for most
operations they follow from the operation. The two that vary carry them in the variant
(`Scope { fails }`, from the body's E, and `Attempt { suspends }`, from `f`'s R).

Scopes (the `Scope` capability value), fiber handles (`Fiber[A]`), Deferreds and causes
(`Cause[E]`) are opaque values chosen by the backend. Capability values may be put in evidence
tables with `Expr::Provide`. Exit (`Std.Fiber`) and CauseKind (`Std.Cause`) are represented like
user enums, with constructor order given by `EXIT_SUCCESS`, `EXIT_FAILURE` and `CAUSE_FAIL`,
`CAUSE_DIE`, `CAUSE_INTERRUPT`.

`Fiber.scope(body)` (spec 11.2). `[body]`, where `body` is a function value taking the
scope capability value. When the body returns a value, the remaining children are
interrupted, and the value is returned after all children finish. The first failure (Fail,
Die) of a child or the body is the scope's result. `fails` tells whether the body's (and
children's) E is not empty.

`s.fork(f)` (spec 11.2). `[scope, f]`, where `f` is a parameterless function value run as
a child fiber. The value is the fiber handle. Not a suspension point (the child starts when
the parent next suspends).
`s.deferred()` (spec 11.7). `[scope]`. The value is an empty Deferred.

`Fiber.join(h)` (spec 11.5). `[fiber]`. The child's value; a defect if the child was
interrupted.
`Fiber.await(h)` (spec 11.5). `[fiber]`. A value of the `exit` enum (`Exit[A, {}]`).

`Fiber.interrupt(h)` (spec 11.4). `[fiber]`. Interrupts the child and waits until it has
unwound. The value is `()`.

`Fiber.attempt(f)` (spec 11.5). `[f]`. Calls `f` on the spot and turns Fail and Die into
`Failure` of the `exit` enum. Interrupt is not caught. `suspends` tells whether `f` may
suspend (the same rule as `Callee::Indirect` of `Expr::Call::suspends`).

`Deferred.complete(d, value)` (spec 11.7). `[deferred, value]`. The value is a Bool. Not a
suspension point.
`Deferred.await(d)` (spec 11.7). `[deferred]`. Waits until a value is set.

`Deferred.poll(d)` (spec 11.7). `[deferred]`. The value is Prelude's Option
(`Module::option_enum`).
`Cause.kind(c)` (spec 11.5). `[cause]`. The value is of the `kind` enum (CauseKind).
`Cause.to_string(c)` (spec 11.5). `[cause]`. `error: …`, `defect: …` or `interrupted`.

`Cause.raise(c)` (spec 11.5). `[cause]`. Fail becomes a failure, Die a defect, and Interrupt
unwinds the current fiber's interruption. The type is Never, but it may fail. `fails` tells
whether the cause's E is not empty.
